title: Uptime monitor & auto-remediation
description: An n8n workflow that health-checks services every 5 minutes, restarts a container that stops answering, verifies the fix, and pages on-call only if it failed. Built by Dyaksa.
intro: A scheduled n8n workflow that health-checks your services, restarts a container that has stopped answering, checks again, and only pages a person if the restart didn't work. Scroll to follow one failed check through all 15 nodes.

stations.title: One node lists everything it watches.
stations.body: Every five minutes a Code node returns one item per service: its name, health URL and container. Adding a service is an edit to that one node, and n8n runs the rest of the graph once per item.
stations.code:
{ json: { service: 'api-gateway', url: 'http://api-gateway:8080/health', container: 'api-gateway' } },
{ json: { service: 'worker-queue', url: 'http://worker-queue:8081/health', container: 'worker-queue' } },

stations.title: A timeout is a result, not a crash.
stations.body: The check returns the full response and never errors, so a 503 is just a status code. A refused connection has no status code at all, which the IF reads as 0: unhealthy. A healthy answer is logged as an up heartbeat, so real uptime can be worked out later.

stations.title: It can restart a container, and nothing else.
stations.body: Restart Container posts to a Docker socket proxy that only allows restarts, so n8n never touches the Docker socket or a shell. A failed restart doesn't stop the run: the re-check still fails and the service is escalated.

stations.title: A restart isn't a fix until it's checked.
stations.body: The workflow waits 30 seconds, then calls the same health URL again. Only that second answer decides what happens next.

stations.title: Fixed by itself: a note, not a page.
stations.body: If the re-check passes, #incidents gets a note that the service recovered after a restart, and the Incidents sheet gets a self_healed row. Nobody is woken up.
check: Still Down After Restart? · false → Notify Self-Healed

stations.title: Still down after a restart? Now a person is paged.
stations.body: On-call is paged in #incidents only after the automatic fix has failed, and an escalated row is logged. Each run restarts once, then escalates. It never loops on a broken deployment.
check: Still Down After Restart? · true → Escalate → Log Incident

stations.title: A silent monitor is worse than none.
stations.body: If the monitor itself breaks, an Error Trigger posts the failed execution's error to #eng-alerts.

stations.title: 15 nodes, three outcomes kept apart.
stations.body: Heartbeat, self-heal and incident are separate log rows. That is what lets you report how many outages fixed themselves and how many needed a person, instead of a single count of alerts.

edgeCases: Service unreachable or the request times out
Treated as unhealthy, not a workflow crash
#incidents note and a Self-Heal log row, no page
On-call escalation and an Incident log row
